result:
PR #307 is marked ready for review and can merge cleanly. The head is `094fff110c`, pushed, with the full selftest at 1501 passed, 0 failed and `preflight.sh` passing outright (no `--allow-tracker` needed). CI on that head hasn't reported yet, and I didn't trigger it.

**Why the earlier sessions didn't finish (now recorded in NOTES.md):** the implementation was never pushed; the real-run script waited for an idle Nova that never came. The last session's run was killed after two minutes when that session ended, because `setsid` doesn't escape the session's process group. This time I kept everything in the foreground and polled until it finished.

**Real Nova run:** Crimson Skies, apk `a00704d02eb0`, run through this branch's own scripts.
- **Verdict:** PASS, a Playable candidate from the 10-minute screening. The route itself marked the gameplay point.
- **Gameplay:** 625 s after `mark gameplay`. The contact sheet shows the plane in flight with its HUD.
- **Frame rate:** at or above 30 fps for 97.2% of gameplay time (median 29.99). 2.19 late frames per 100, worst stall 328 ms.
- **Audio:** 0.029% short callbacks, against a 0.1% bar.
- **Crash / hang:** none. 6 adb failures, none mistaken for the game exiting.

The artifacts are in `docs/lanes/titlerun/realrun/`.

It took three tries, because each earlier try hit a problem that only shows on a real device. Each fix has a selftest case, and each case fails if its fix is removed:
- **Every liveness check failed:** the Nova's `ps` pads its `NAME` header with trailing spaces, so the soak never saw the game as running. Trailing blanks are now stripped.
- **One adb failure silenced the whole run:** a single WSL `UtilAcceptVsock` error meant pad detection found nothing, so no input was played, and it also killed the logcat stream, so `logcat.txt` was empty. Pad detection now retries three times. The logcat stream restarts from the newest line, so frame windows aren't counted twice, and each gap is written to `run.log`.
- **Pace was always null:** the verdict looked for words the `hakuX-pace` line never contains. It now reads the line's fields in the format agreed with lane.perfbase, and the run was re-judged.

Two master selftests read `dispatcher.sh`'s snapshot code as text, and my change to that function broke both. I kept master's lines as they were rather than edit those two tests, which aren't in this lane's files.

Two route presses in the passing run were lost to adb errors; a failed route step is logged and skipped, not retried. The Nova hold was lifted when the run ended, and no device setting was changed. PR 2 (Galleon, DOA3 and JSRF routes on the Thor) is next.
